text.aria-label: Title text 'An era is a period during which one version of the weather forecast product ran. The study has no 2026-01, so the later era starts at 2026-02. Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. The primary hyperparameter setting is depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8. The screening rule picked AN from the first 10 months, so AN's row here is out of sample. All rows are post hoc: written after the first run's results were known. Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. PC: the 7-day ratio of power to CAMS satellite irradiance, and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use.'
text.tspan: An era is a period during which one version of the weather forecast product ran. The study has no 2026-01, so the later era
starts at 2026-02. Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. The primary hyperparameter setting is
depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8.
The screening rule picked AN from the first 10 months, so AN's row here is out of sample.
All rows are post hoc: written after the first run's results were known.
Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. PC: the 7-day ratio of power to CAMS satellite irradiance, and the 30-day ratio of CAMS
to forecast irradiance. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. TF: the 30-day ratio
of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. L1: B0
plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a
day-ahead forecast). AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky
irradiance, on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. L2: L1 plus that hour's
weather forecast. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier
(keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual
over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a
first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. CK: the
plant's clipping ceiling. IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other
plants. T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from
months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use.
